main_text.p: oportere consentiunt omnes nostri: etiam Calvinistæ. Subscripserunt enim unanimes huic sententiæ: Harmon. confess. fid. sect. 16. Helvet. poster. Fidelium corpora, ut Spiritus sancti templa, & quæ in ultimo die recte creduntur resurrectura, iubet Scriptura honestè absque superstitione humo mandare. Atqui honestè ieiunare corpora, est ea honorare: sicut De eccles. triumph. lib. 1. cap. 4. Bellarminus docet è Scriptura & Hieronymo, dicens: Deuteronomy ultimo, Deus ipse (ut Hieronymus contra Vigilantium argumentatur) corpus Moysis honoravit, dum illud propriis manibus sepelivit. Nostri igitur omnes honorari debere sanctorum corpora consentiunt. Ac Moysis, Num. 11. 7. viri Deo longè acceptissimi, quo nihil habuit antiqua ætas mitius, sapientius, sanctius, teste Præfat. de ecc. triumph. Bellarmino, corpus nullo alio honore est affectum, quàm ut' sepeliretur. Ita quem honorem haberi voluit Deus sanctissimi viri corpori: eum corporibus omnium Sanctorum habendum statuunt nostri.

2 Nec verò adversantur huic assertioni testimonia Lutheri, Magdeburgensium, Calvini, à Bellarmino producta. Etenim honorem & cultum Pontificium ac superstitiosum reliquiis illi denegant, ut Deut. 34. 6. antè declaravi: sed pium & Christianum honorem non denegant. Immò Luthetus iis ipsis verbis quæ Bellarminus citat è Sermone de cruce, reliquias nempe altissime sub terram abscondendas, quid aliud aliorum Sanctorum corporibus faciendum censet, quàm divinitus corpori Moysis factum est? Magdeburgenses item, qui passim reprehendunt cultum reliquiarum, sed præcipuè Centuria quarta, capite sexto, columna 456. ut ait Bellarminus: nonne ibidem evidenter indicant reliquias honorificè humandas sibi videri?

page.notes: Marginal notes in the right margin are small italic references and were transcribed as printed but partly abbreviated by the reader; the letter marks f (Cap. I. §. 11) and the "&c." after Cap. I are in the margin near the second paragraph. Several words in the right-margin notes are uncertain (e.g. "Harmon.", "triumph.") and the marks a–e may not all match. Line 2 of the notes ("sect. 16") is partly illegible. Words at the end of the main text ("honorem", "sepeliretur") are read from the scan with some doubt. The text of the first column is set in a roman face with Latin spelling; the lower-left "Ferè" of the mid-page is not clearly printed. Some words such as "affectum" and "superstitiosum" are not certain. Leading "2" is a paragraph number, not a heading.
